2. Use Google calendar. It's somewhat inconvenient to switch between 2 apps all the time though

So I can give only 4 stars due to this inconvenience.

body: Surprised that a leading software company developed this product without the functionality of sharing between users, ie., "shared task lists." It integrates with their calendar product - a software our household uses to manage various agendas. The calendar product allows me to open tasks, to add a task to calendar, but its isolated to only the one user - both in Tasks and in Calendar. The only supported shared function is events in Calendar. Surprising functionality decision. It would be a better product if it were developed further to: 1) create shared lists with other users, and 2) incorporate visibility/public settings to share your task lists the way users can share their calendars.

title: Please add these features
body:
1. Export task list to textable/emailable/ doc format
2. Please allow a task created in the main list to be assigned to a space, not to need to create the task within spaces. Furthermore, create the ability to move a task from one space to another, or to populate multiple spaces.
3. Add Subtask feature to tasks within spaces as well, just as it does in the main task list.
4. Allow to create task templates for repeated work flows,  both in main task and within spaces.
5. Integrate tasks with google sheets. Allow a spreadsheet field to convert to a linkable task, by right clicking. Furthermore, allow an entire task list template to create a spreadsheet (with gantt template would be awesome). Allow the task template to populate the spreadsheet with the whole templated task list.  This would allow for pipeline work flows that are repateable and easily created. 

Overall, a good app, but with the amazing new spaces, and the robust google sheets, the lack of integration is stoping the task feature from being 5 stars.

title: Not giving notifications and not persistent notifications.
body:
I really want to like and use this app. I deleted it a few months ago due to not being able to add repeating tasks or assign a time to a task. Now you add both of those. I also recall last version the notifications would not persist. Like you hear the ding. Then pull down the menu to look see it. Turn off the phone screen and turn it on again and it’s gone. Again, useless! Have completed the task yet and still need to see the reminder!

I’m kind of mad now that yesterday I deleted all my tasks from iOS reminders app when I installed this latest version due to the new features I wanted. Now I want to go back...iOS reminders app is flawless and the reminders are persistent in the drop down menu.

title: What is the point?
body:
“One of the world’s richest companies writing one of the least capable apps.”  That should be the tag line.

We use Google’s tasks throughout our day, every day.  We use both the web version and the service through through GoTasks (which I, unfortunately, no longer see on the AppStore).

The web version is simple and works well.  This version has been out for how long?  It only now supports the iPad, and it still doesn’t support the basic functionality of Google’s web version. Where are the sub items, never mind the other basic service features.  It’s support for sub items is to flatten my list?  When I add a new item, sometimes the text area shows up so I can see what I’m typing, aaaand sometimes it doesn’t.

I could go on, but what’s the point?  It’s simpler to abandon this app and find something that isn’t a joke.  After all, given the ridiculously minimal amount of attention Google has given it, aren’t they simply going to abandon it, too?  After all, it’s what they do!

Google:  look at GoTasks, if you can find it. It’s so much simpler and elegant, and, yet, so much more capable...with your own service!

title: Good but there are a few things missing
body: This app looks good and does what it's suppposed to, but there are a few things that prevent me from switching over from google keep. The first one is geofenced notifications, and the second thing is that if you mark a task with subtasks (or a subtask) as complete, every subtask becomes a regular task and if you uncheck it, it does not return to it's parent list, it just goes back as a regular task. This is super annoying.
author: christiangnrd

title: This app so lean I shouldn’t have to list for free
body:
This is the leanest to do app you’re gonna ever get.

It’s actually more like a sheet of paper, but on your phone. Out of the box you’re getting a stripped down wunderlist, and when I say stripped, I mean stripped. Say hello to no notifications, no shareable links, no tagging, no calendar sync, no useable web version, no bells, no whistles, no, no, no.

“Hey but does it have collabora...” no.
“But does it have google assistant integrat...” no.
“Ah but does it hav...” no.

What it does have is simple tasks & sub tasks, with due dates. Like a list your mom used to write on the table with a pencil.

If you’re reading this Google, ship these features to make tasks 1000x better:

1. Add shareable links (no login required)
2. Add tagging
3. Make a useable web ui.

All that said, it’s kind of refreshing to use such a simple app. You know how to use it immediately out of the box without even thinking. Come to think of it, I’ve created 3 lists within the last hour & haven’t thought twice about whether I was doing it “correctly” or not.

No features to get lost in which is nice. Does a simple thing & does it well. 5 stars.
